messages.subject: Covariance constraint between latent variables
parts:
Dear all,

I'm new to R and Lavaan and currently trying to estimate a model in which certain parameters are restricted. This seems to work fine until I estimate a model in which I restrict a covariance between two latent variable to a certain value:
LatentA ~~ 0.499*LatentB

Lavaan is returning: 
Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters.


It seems to me that Lavaan is specifically having problems with this restrictions (as the model is normally fitted when deleting this constraint, and adding other (non-convariance) constraints doesn't result in any problems too). Anyone an idea on how to solve this? Thanks in advance!

When you freely estimate that covariance, what is the estimated value?  0.499 is a pretty specific value, but there isn't enough information to diagnose a problem (assuming it is actually a problem and not just evidence of a poorly chosen constraint).  Posting your full syntax and relevant summary output might help.

> Dear all,
>
> I'm new to R and Lavaan and currently trying to estimate a model in
> which certain parameters are restricted. This seems to work fine until I
> estimate a model in which I restrict a covariance between two latent
> variable to a certain value:
> LatentA ~~ 0.499*LatentB
>
> Lavaan is returning:
>
> Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats =
> lavsamplestats, : lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is
> not positive definite; check your model and/or starting parameters.

Have you read the error message: your initial (and user-specified)
parameter values imply a covariance matrix for the observed variables
that is not positive definite.

It is a bit silly to constrain covariances, but not variances. The
initial starting values for latent variances are 0.05. A covariance of
0.499 will not work.

Or is 0.499 a correlation? Then, have you used std.lv = TRUE?

Yves.

messages.author: 0a90d9aa4e77339c
messages.subject: Re: Covariance constraint between latent variables
parts:
Dear Terrence and Yves,

Thanks for the fast replies. Without the constraint, the covariance was estimated to be 0.499. Providing starting values for the variances of the latent variables solved my problem.
